rule: Skip one-time comparisons; record why. Do not exclude ordinary reusable collocations solely because they are compositional.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Violent crime can shake the ground beneath society.
rows.reason: The source applies a bespoke earthquake image to violent crime and social safety. “Shake the ground beneath society” is not a stable transferable unit; this decision does not exclude a separately evidenced idiom such as “shake the foundations.”
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: For many users, the rules keep changing while they are still learning the game.
rows.exactExpression: rules keep changing while they are still learning the game
rows.reason: The full changing-rules analogy is custom, but “learn the game” figuratively means mastering how a system works, and the source directly applies that reusable game frame to digital systems. The exclusion rule alone cannot close this row; keep it held for a source-faithful re-lemma/owner check, without promoting a lesson automatically.
rows.nextGate: retain hold; source-faithful re-lemma and owner/teaching-value review

rows.exactSourceSentence: Even gentle walks remind us the body was made to move.
rows.exactExpression: the body was made to move
rows.reason: “The body was made to move” is a source-specific fitness maxim. It states the speaker’s belief about exercise; no bounded expression or contrastive learner decision survives transfer beyond that slogan.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: After the injury, she learned it was better to move wisely than to push recklessly.
rows.exactExpression: move wisely than to push recklessly
rows.reason: The after-injury sentence sets up a tailored wise-versus-reckless comparison. “Move wisely” and “push recklessly” are ordinary verbal choices, while the contrast is the one-time teaching point.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: The broadcast felt like a circus with too many rings.
rows.exactExpression: a circus with too many rings
rows.reason: The exact “circus with too many rings” wording is inventive, but it is a recognizable extension of the established figurative “three-ring circus” for confused, crowded activity. Keep held pending an exact-source variant/teaching-value check; neither automatic exclusion nor automatic lesson promotion is justified.
rows.nextGate: retain hold; source-faithful re-lemma and owner/teaching-value review

rows.exactSourceSentence: A good academy aims to train the person, not just the body.
rows.exactExpression: train the person, not just the body
rows.reason: “Train the person, not just the body” is a tailored academy mission contrast between whole-person education and physical training. The whole contrast, rather than a reusable lexical unit, conveys the source point.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: Science moves faster when minds meet across borders.
rows.exactExpression: science moves faster when minds meet
rows.reason: The cross-border science sentence coins a collaboration maxim by coupling faster-moving science with minds meeting. “Minds meet” is understandable, but this particular compressed causal image is not a bounded course expression; exclude only the source construction.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: Writing is like laying a thought down carefully.
rows.reason: The explicit “Writing is like…” comparison invents an image of physically laying down a thought. The expression has no independent stable sense apart from this analogy.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason

rows.exactSourceSentence: The luxury car looked like a statement on wheels.
rows.reason: The luxury-car line turns the car into a “statement on wheels,” a tailored prestige image. “Statement” or “on wheels” can be reused separately, but the combined unit is the one-time analogy and does not establish its own seven-step target.
rows.nextGate: documented non-course exclusion, preserving source and reason
